title: Check: a method that scales
description: Five questions on working from symptom to component.

questions.prompt: A Pod is not serving traffic. What is the highest-value first command?

options.text: kubectl describe pod, for status and events

questions.explanation: Status plus events tells you whether it was ever scheduled, whether the image pulled and whether probes pass - before you go looking at logs.

options.text: The Pod has not been bound to a node

questions.explanation: Pending is a scheduling story: resources, taints, affinity or an unbound PVC. ContainerCreating is the phase where images pull and volumes mount.

questions.prompt: Which check splits a Service problem in half fastest?

options.text: Whether the Service has ready endpoints

questions.explanation: Endpoints present means look at the network path; endpoints absent means look at labels and readiness.

questions.prompt: Traffic fails from outside but works from inside the cluster. Where do you look?

options.text: The ingress path: controller, Ingress rules and the external load balancer

questions.explanation: Working internally proves Pods, Services and DNS. The fault is in what sits in front of them.

questions.prompt: What is the first question to ask about any sudden failure?

options.text: What changed - a rollout, a config edit, an upgrade?

questions.explanation: Most incidents are a recent change. `kubectl rollout history` and the events answer it faster than reasoning from first principles.
